subject: Priv deploy IaC: environment parameterization and module interop review
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jared Mills <jared@acme-fin.com>
Date: Sat, 04 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Priv deploy IaC: environment parameterization and module interop review

Hi team,

I pulled together a short summary of the problem Acme flagged during the pre-prod smoke: our terraform modules, helm charts, and ansible playbooks each expect environment-specific data in slightly different shapes, which has been causing drift between staging/prod values and failing compliance evidence checks. Acme called out two concrete failures last week: 1) inconsistent CIDR/egress policy values between tf and helm leading to unreachable webhook endpoints, and 2) secrets leaking into rendered helm values during a GitLab pipeline run.

Objective for this thread: align on a minimal interface contract between TF modules, Helm values, and Ansible roles, plus CI gating checks that provide audit evidence (signatures for template rendering + a canonical values snapshot).

Proposed next steps (short):
- Agree a single "module interface" doc (attached tf-module-interface.md).
- Add a small canonical values file per env (priv-iac-sample-values.yaml) stored in the secure artifacts bucket; pipelines reference it rather than ad-hoc env vars.
- Enforce CI checks: template-diff + secret-scan + signed-artifact proof (ci-pipeline-snippets.patch).

Can Kimberly and Karthik review the attached interface doc and give red/amber/green on feasibility? Jared - is this approach acceptable for Acme's auditors (they want a deterministic source of truth for env values)?

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Product Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: tf-module-interface.md (text), priv-iac-sample-values.yaml (yaml), ci-pipeline-snippets.patch (diff)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jared Mills <jared@acme-fin.com>
Date: Sat, 04 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priv deploy IaC: environment parameterization and module interop review

On Sat, Apr 4, 2026 at 9:12 AM Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com> wrote:
> Objective for this thread: align on a minimal interface contract between TF modules, Helm values, and Ansible roles, plus CI gating checks that provide audit evidence (signatures for template rendering + a canonical values snapshot).

+1 on the approach. A few immediate implementation notes from the dedicated infra team:
- The TF modules should expose a small set of exported outputs that the Helm render job consumes via a templated values file (not environment interpolation). We already have an internal library to convert TF outputs -> helm values; we should reuse that to avoid custom glue.
- For secrets, do NOT write them into the Helm values files. Use a placeholder token and let the Ansible role inject secrets at runtime from KMS (we can produce an audit log for the inject step).
- CI proof: I like the signed-artifact approach. We need to make sure the signing key is in an HSM-backed KMS and the pipeline records the signature and the artifact checksum in the build metadata.

I'll review tf-module-interface.md and push comments inline by EOD Monday.

K
Kimberly Park
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood

Attachment note: I added an example snippet to ci-pipeline-snippets.patch showing how we sign the artifact in GitLab.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jared Mills <jared@acme-fin.com>, SaaS Infra <infra@cloudpartner.io>
Date: Sun, 05 Apr 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priv deploy IaC: environment parameterization and module interop review

Thanks Priyom — good framing. A few technical details from the module side:

- Module boundary: we should treat TF as the source of truth for network/topology (VPCs, subnets, routing, egress) and publish a small JSON artifact per run (tf-output.json) that downstream Helm/Ansible jobs consume. This artifact must be immutable and signed by the TF pipeline.
- Helm charts should be templated to accept that JSON artifact and map values explicitly (no implicit overrides). We need a helper utility (we can add a small binary or templating helper) to perform the mapping during the render stage.
- Ansible roles should be idempotent and parameterized to accept final runtime secrets via a vault lookup (not pipeline envs).

CI gating: add a job that performs a strict compatibility check: given tf-output.json and the helm values mapping, render both staging and prod and compare endpoints/egress/CIDR lists. If there is any mismatch, fail the merge with a detailed diff file attached to the MR.

I've opened a draft PR with the mapping helper and a test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/priv-iac/pull/218

I'll sync with CloudPartner infra (cc'd) on the signing KMS integration; they handle HSM in Acme's environment.

- Karthik

Attachment: sample unit test logs in the PR.

From: Jared Mills <jared@acme-fin.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: SaaS Infra <infra@cloudpartner.io>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Apr 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priv deploy IaC: environment parameterization and module interop review

Thanks — this looks like the kind of determinism our auditors want. A couple of clarifying points from Acme:
- The auditors will want a documented chain-of-custody for the tf-output.json (who signed it, pipeline id, timestamp). Can the TF pipeline include metadata and publish to the secure artifacts bucket we agreed on?
- For secrets, we will require that no secret material appears in any artifact in plaintext (even placeholders that resolve to secrets in some environments). Placeholders are ok if they are non-reversible tokens.

If you can share an example signed artifact and the CI job name that will validate it, our audit folks can pre-approve the pattern and avoid a follow-up evidence request.

Regards,
Jared
Cloud Ops Lead, Acme Financial Services

On a process note — can we have the compatibility check added to the protected branch merge rule so no MR can be merged without the check passing?

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jared Mills <jared@acme-fin.com>, SaaS Infra <infra@cloudpartner.io>
Date: Mon, 06 Apr 2026 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priv deploy IaC: environment parameterization and module interop review

All — quick status and action items after reading the thread and the draft PR:

1) Action (Karthik): add the tf-output.json signer metadata (pipeline_id, builder_id, timestamp, key-id). Small change in the TF pipeline; estimate 1 day.
2) Action (Kimberly): update ci-pipeline-snippets.patch to include an explicit protected-branch gate (reject merge if compatibility-check job not present).
3) Action (Priyom): create an audit evidence template (one-page) that Acme can attach to their SOC process — include the chain-of-custody fields Jared requested.
4) Action (Jared/CloudPartner): confirm that HSM/KMS key-id can be referenced by pipeline and accepted by Acme auditors (reply by COB Wed).

I will track these as JIRA-ACME-4312 subtasks and request a compliance pre-review once items 1–3 are in a branch.

Thanks everyone — looks like we have a clear, low-risk path forward.

Neha Kapoor
Manager, Compliance Engineering, Redwood Inference
